answer: Each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can transact, and a public ledger records every commitment. If an agent signs conflicting commitments, anyone can submit both signatures as proof and trigger the loss of its deposit. A pulse of fake identities therefore requires capital for each account; a plume of conflicting orders can burn those deposits. The rule raises the cost of flooding the market, though an attacker with an ocean of capital can still participate.
